meaning: FileStore physical access is insufficient for stable artifact identity; study proposes a layered data/result plane.
Workspace, path-based store, immutable blob, artifact, manifest/catalog, raw source snapshot and materialization have different semantic identity.
Existing FileStore is an appropriate low-level port, not a source of result/provenance lifecycle authority.
Large files, multiple backends, error truth, crash safety and portable identities are proposal-specific functional/nonfunctional requirements.
Path-only, sidecar metadata, artifact catalog over FileStore, full object-store and event-sourcing offer different costs; research prefers bounded catalog.
Candidate ArtifactService, content store, catalog and mutable Workspace plus separate cache/staging have different ownership.
Small portable file operations and explicit capabilities are proposed rather than a universal path/database object.
Backends should disclose streaming/seek/range limits and avoid mandatory whole-object RAM buffering for large inputs.
POSIX behaviors such as atomic rename do not generalize to all storage adapters; capability discovery is needed for safe strategies.
Distinguish missing, denied, unavailable, conflict, unsupported, corrupted and partial effects; use portable storage locators.
Optional filesystem abstraction adapter may help, but importing a third-party abstraction as all of product semantics is unwarranted.
Content digest, blob references and optional CAS reduce path coupling; digest collision, retention and physical backend constraints still need verification.
Logical artifact ID, descriptors, parts and versioned manifest differ from a filename; UI-only flags belong outside immutable manifest.
Staging, committed, quarantined, tombstoned and garbage collected have different effects; a second-phase delete protects referenced bytes.
Stage, close, hash, verify, persist blobs/manifest, catalog commit, then expose artifact; filesystem rename alone insufficient across backends.
Workspace files can change, managed artifact content should not change in-place; not every scratch workspace file is an artifact.
Raw-source snapshot must preserve exact fetched bytes and publisher/fetch semantics, linking to but distinct from general artifact object.
Entity/activity/actor provenance and run input-output relations cannot be reconstructed from folder names or timestamps alone.
Metadata index improves queries; local relational catalog is one physical option, portable manifest is separate. SQLite/WAL suitability depends on mode.
Canonical artifact metadata must be independent of client display/projection fields; clients reference stable IDs instead of copied ownership.
Remote/mobile clients may consume descriptors/parts through a transport, not server filesystem paths; external host features are conditional.
Machine consumers should receive restricted artifact/operation capabilities; scratch and derivation provenance need bounded authority.
Content immutability differs from permanent retention; classification, integrity checks, quarantine and access policy remain requirements to decide.
Cache is recomputable, artifact truth is durable; cache identity must include versioned operation/input/registry meanings.
Composite manifest is portable across filesystems/object stores; logical bundle differs from ZIP physical packaging.
Canonical datasets may exist before Excel; operation result should distinguish substantive result, artifacts and declared effects.
Analytic core should expose neutral storage/artifact contracts without reproducing environment-specific implementation data.
Proposed packages and clients are candidate physical layouts; artifact identity has headless consumers and cannot be owned only by desktop.
Immutable artifact metadata, operational visibility/lifecycle and per-user UI preferences require separate owners.
Flexible artifact kinds, derived preview and searchable catalog are capabilities that should remain independently testable.
Reference-aware GC and staging lease recovery require explicit retention rules and crash-time reconciliation.
Logical catalog publication and fenced resource conflicts matter more than assuming all storage backends are atomically renameable.
Manifest/provenance schemas need versioning; artifact catalog must not silently absorb all case/history/application truth.
Fetch official source, fix raw snapshot, compute, export and publish demonstrates possible lineage without proving implementation.
The study rejects path identity, unsafe copy-delete, hidden fallback and monolithic FileStore; physical CAS recommendation is a choice, not accepted.
Node-owned workspace/artifact areas and separate metadata/payload are physical candidate layouts tied to deployment.
Eight stages of contracts, blob service, catalog, data operations, provenance, clients, remote and machine permissions form unapproved Research sequence.
FileStore conformance, artifact immutability, crash windows and fault injection are candidate tests; none run here.
Typed artifact events and a multi-owner responsibility table are proposals requiring adopted boundaries and policies.
Sixteen recommended design choices include CAS, local metadata database, manifests, immutable artifacts and optional filesystem adapter; none Product-admitted.
Proof-bearing object model restated against path-only product; roadmap is derivative and not a Commission.
External filesystem/content/artifact/provenance references support conceptual comparison, not current implementation or compliance certification.
